causalHypotheses: The promotion journal is asked to be simultaneously untrusted portable input and the sole record of pre-promotion reality; since an attacker controlling a portable case controls every file, no file-local predicate can distinguish a forged applied/original=false/live-present entry from the legitimate promotion of a brand-new artifact, so deletion decisions keyed on the self-asserted original bit are unsound by construction (F1, F9), and the mirror flaw — rollback mutating the world without journalizing per-entry progress — yields genuine states the validator rejects forever (F8).

AC7's whole-case no-symlink guarantee was implemented as a library primitive plus per-entry-point discipline instead of a mandatory chokepoint on the public write API; create_case/resume_case/phase_event remember the order, fork_case/run_attempts/log_event forgot it, so the four containment blockers are instances of one missing architectural guarantee rather than four bugs.

The cycle-2 seams were authored to demonstrate planned behavior rather than discriminate contract from accident: each fabricates a state the production machinery cannot reach or omits the branch-distinct input, so the suite stays green while the genuinely reachable second-interruption state deterministically bricks recovery — the seams did not merely miss F8, they concealed it.

All three families follow from one unstated default: durability artifacts (promotion.json, events.jsonl, state.json) and caller-supplied paths are treated as trusted internal records at some sites and untrusted input at others, wherever convenient; making that trust boundary explicit per artifact would have surfaced every blocker in this union.

findingVotes.rationale: Verified: forged applied/original=false journal passes _validate_recovery_artifacts' else-branch and rollback's discard_workspace(live) deletes phase-owned data/sources.json. Decisive impossibility argument: the forged state is extensionally identical to a legitimately promoted new artifact, so no confined predicate separates them; only a fail-closed destructive rule (destroy only what a held/corroborated backup proves the promoter moved) fixes it. Causal-subgraph-reconstruction.

fork_case resolves dest before scanning only the source; copytree lands the child under the symlink target. The containment primitive and canonical scan-unresolved-first order already exist in create_case; scanning the unresolved destination before resolve is a one-point confined repair that also closes F7. Known invariant, lapsed enforcement — not evidence for reconstruction on its own.

_gate_input strip-checks the actor but only emptiness-checks sequence members, so ['   '] derives gate capability; Gate A burns attempts failing inside approve_detector_plan while Gate B seals an empty accepted set and completes P7 — completion without a human decision, violating the locked pauses-consume-no-attempts contract. Mirroring actor.strip() onto items plus value-table rows is confined-repair.

Every exit path, including the BaseException handler, persists failure evidence before unwinding, so the test's caught KeyboardInterrupt can never reach _reconcile_interrupted_attempt's missing-evidence branch — the exact branch AC2 added for hard termination. The seam must synthesize a counted attempt with no failure.json and prove deterministic evidence synthesis plus the bounded stop. test-contract-repair.

Ordered _apply persists each entry applied before advancing, so the fixture's pending-prefix/applied-last journal with only the last backup is unreachable; the test certifies rollback of an impossible state while reachable shapes go untested — it directly masked F8. Rebuild as a real applied-prefix (drive promote_workspace under interruption or construct prefix-consistent artifacts/backups). test-contract-repair.

_completion_identity demonstrably hashes chart descendants by relative path, kind, and bytes, so no live misbehavior is shown; the gap is regression-proofing. Add descendant add/change/remove/kind-mutation rows to P7_OUTPUT_MUTATIONS asserting invalidated_from == P7 and README demotion. Coverage debt, not a defect: blocking false, test-contract-repair.

Standards-lens duplicate of F2 with the identical resolution point (scan the unresolved destination before resolve); one confined repair closes both. Council should count it once against the containment family rather than as an independent defect — direct evidence the union is not eleven independent faults.

Rollback restores applied-original entries by consuming backups without journalizing progress and persists rolled_back only after the loop; a second interruption leaves applied/original/backup-absent/live-restored, which validation rejects on every subsequent restart — deterministic permanent bricking through ordinary double-crash use. Ad hoc acceptance of that shape is unsound because it collides with forged F1-shaped states; rollback must become resumable with journaled restore-progress inside the same reconstructed recovery machine as F1/F9.

Identical mechanism to F1 aimed at README.md; project_readme returns early on a missing file, so rollback-deleted journalist-authored content is unrecoverable. Highest-severity member of the same trust-model defect, sharing both the reconstruction remedy and the impossibility argument (legitimate new-artifact promotion is locally indistinguishable from the forgery).

Documented public run_attempts calls load_snapshot, whose durable tree mkdir/state/event writes precede any _scan_case_tree, and its only later scan inspects the copied workspace, not the caller path — AC7 requires every public write path protected. Hoisting the existing scan to entry, as phase_event already does, is confined-repair; nothing beyond the chokepoint question needs redesign.

Standalone log_event mkdir+append follows symlinked ancestors with no scan; the decorator's scan misses direct callers, and the broad handler fails safe only when the redirected write errors — a successful out-of-case append returns normally. Scanning inside log_event and mapping UnsafeCasePathError to the documented None return preserves never-raise. confined-repair.

inquiry.problemRestatement: Are these independent defects, or evidence that this part of the design should be reconstructed? Concretely: do the promotion-journal trust model, the unchoked public write surface, and the non-binding test seams reduce to one design decision — treating durability artifacts and caller paths as trusted records wherever convenient — such that F1/F8/F9 require reconstructing the promotion-recovery state machine around fail-closed destructive rules, F2/F7/F10/F11 and F3 admit confined repairs through the existing containment and validation primitives, and F4/F5/F6 require rebuilding the seams to bind to genuinely reachable production states? — Eleven survived cycle-2 blockers form three families over one substrate. Trust model (F1, F8, F9): recovery validates journal schema and registry binding but trusts the journal's claims about the world; a forged applied/original=false/no-backup entry passes the 'coherent = not backup.exists()' branch and rollback deletes the live registry-bound artifact (data/sources.json; README.md with unrecoverable journalist content), while rollback's own unjournaled progress creates legitimate states the same validator permanently rejects on every restart. Containment (F2/F7, F10, F11): the _scan_case_tree primitive and its canonical scan-unresolved-path-before-resolve-or-write order exist (create_case, resume_case, phase_event), yet fork_case resolves dest before any destination scan, run_attempts writes durable state before any scan and afterwards scans only the copied workspace, and standalone log_event never scans. Seams (F4, F5, F6): the interrupted-attempt test only produces evidence-backed interruptions so the missing-evidence reconcile branch is unreachable, the promotion fixture fabricates an applied-last/pending-prefix journal the sequential applier cannot produce, and the P7 matrix never mutates a chart descendant, leaving descendant-hash invalidation unpinned.
inquiry.question: Are these independent defects, or evidence that this part of the design should be reconstructed?

src/anomaly/_attempt_workspace.py: _apply persists each entry 'applied' before advancing while _rollback journalizes no per-entry progress and writes 'rolled_back' only after the loop; validation accepts original entries only via backup.exists() or (applying and live.exists()), so the reachable mid-rollback shape (applied, original, backup consumed, live restored) raises WorkflowError on every future restart (F8) while apply-time interruptions remain recoverable.

src/anomaly/workflow_inputs.py _gate_input applies actor.strip() but only 'not item' to sequence members, so ['   '] is capability-complete for both gates; per refute-final-3 the Gate B path then finds no matching claim, writes findings and the gate-b receipt from an empty accepted set, and completes P7 — whitespace input converts the human boundary into an empty seal.

tests/test_pipeline_walk.py: the interruption loop (:615-621) raises only caught KeyboardInterrupts whose evidence run_attempts persists before unwinding, so the missing-evidence reconcile branch is unreachable (F4); the promotion fixture (:652-664) marks only entries[-1] applied with earlier entries pending, unreachable by ordered _apply (F5); P7_OUTPUT_MUTATIONS (:196-215) rmtree's the whole charts directory but never mutates a descendant (F6) — three green seams with zero discriminating power while the reachable F8 state bricks recovery.

inquiry.question: Deletion authority over registry-bound artifacts currently derives from an untrusted journal's own original=false assertion, the same validator permanently rejects genuinely mid-rollback states, and the whole-case no-symlink boundary is enforced at create/resume but skipped by fork destination resolution, run_attempts pre-write durable state, and standalone log_event — should each site get its local guard while the promotion-recovery authorization alone is rebuilt on filesystem-verified provenance plus journalized rollback progress? Are these independent defects, or evidence that this part of the design should be reconstructed?
inquiry.problemRestatement: Eleven surviving cycle-2 blockers at gated hash 429c34de collapse, under independent code verification, into four causal clusters. (a) Journal-asserted deletion authority: _validate_recovery_artifacts accepts a non-rolled-back entry with original=false solely because the backup is absent, never requiring the live target to be absent, and _rollback then calls discard_workspace(live) — so a schema-valid, registry-bound forged journal deletes a legitimate P1 artifact (F1) or the journalist-authored README.md during public restart (F9, irreversible because project_readme returns when README.md is missing); reachability runs through the ordinary public dispatcher, which resumes any regular-file portable case before recovering the journal. (b) Recovery liveness: _rollback restores applied originals by consuming their backups without journalizing per-entry progress, so a second interruption mid-rollback leaves an applied/original/no-backup/live shape the validator rejects on every subsequent restart (F8). (c) Symlink boundary incompleteness: fork_case resolves dest before any scan and copies into the resolved external path (F2, re-raised as F7); run_attempts loads and durably writes snapshot state through a symlinked root before its only scan, which examines the copied workspace afterward (F10); standalone log_event mkdirs and appends through case-controlled symlinks with no scan at all (F11). (d) Validation and proof gaps: _gate_input applies .strip() to the actor but not to sequence IDs, so whitespace-only Gate A/B selections count as complete human decisions and can consume attempts or seal an empty accepted P7 set (F3); the interrupted-attempt test always records evidence via the BaseException handler so the missing-evidence reconciliation branch is never exercised (F4); the valid-rollback fixture's pending-prefix/applied-last journal is unreachable from the sequential promoter (F5); and the P7 matrix removes only the whole charts directory, leaving descendant-content invalidation unproven (F6).
causalHypotheses: The promotion validator substitutes schema and registry-shape checking for provenance verification: it trusts the journal's own original flag instead of testing the asserted pre-promotion existence against the live tree, making deletion authority forgeable by anyone who can place a file in a portable case (F1, F9).

Rollback mutates live files and consumes backups without persisting per-entry progress, so crash windows produce intermediate states that the validator's producer-shaped invariants classify as incoherent — the same validator is simultaneously too permissive toward forgeries and too strict toward genuine progress, indicating the recovery state machine's invariants were derived per-case rather than from one verified model (F8, and the laxness F1/F9 exploit).

Containment is implemented per-writer rather than as a single entry-point invariant: create_case and resume_case scan before touching disk, but fork_case resolved its destination first, run_attempts performs durable writes before any scan, and log_event ships with no scan — AC7's 'every public resume/read/write path' was satisfied entry-by-entry instead of structurally (F2, F7, F10, F11).

Gate predicates validate presence, type, uniqueness, and separators but normalize only the actor field; sequence IDs miss the same .strip() discipline, so whitespace-only selections masquerade as decisions at the human turn boundary (F3).

Test fixtures synthesize journal states by editing individual fields instead of replaying producer sequences, yielding unreachable shapes (pending prefix with applied tail) and assertions that cannot distinguish content-hash identity from existence-only checks (F4, F5, F6).

Verified at test_pipeline_walk.py:644-672 against _apply (:82-104): the promoter persists each entry applying→applied strictly in write order, so a journal with three pending entries and only the events tail applied — backed by a single backup — is unreachable; validation imposes no prefix-order guard, which is exactly the laxness F1/F9 weaponize. Verified that identities._completion_identity recursively enumerates findings/charts and hashes each descendant's relative path, kind, and bytes, so a mutated chart descendant does invalidate P7 today; the matrix at test_pipeline_walk.py:196-215 merely fails to prove it, and its rmtree-only mutation cannot distinguish content hashing from existence checks. Still require one matrix row mutating a chart descendant's bytes/kind as cheap conformance insurance for the publication-truth invariant.

Same code site and identical mechanism as F2, re-derived under the standards lens; independent verification confirms dest resolution precedes any containment check and copytree follows the resolved external path. The lens duplication does not dilute the underlying hole — one confined destination scan fixes both findings, but until it lands, a public writer remains outside the locked no-symlink contract. Blocks alongside F2; tracked separately only so neither review record can be closed while the escape survives.

Verified at _rollback (:109-131): each non-pending original entry is restored via backup.replace(live) with no journal write inside the loop, and the rolled_back status lands only after all entries; _validate_recovery_artifacts (:244-256) then demands backup.exists() (or applying+live) for applied originals, so a second interruption mid-rollback leaves applied/original/no-backup/live — rejected with WorkflowError on every future restart, permanently locking the case out of recovery. Fail-closed-forever is an availability defect reachable by ordinary crash timing, not just adversaries. Confined fix: journalize per-entry rollback progress (or accept restored-original-no-backup-live-exists as coherent and complete the rollback idempotently).

Worst instance of the F1 root cause, verified end-to-end: P7's registry tuple includes README.md; a forged applied/original=false/no-backup README entry passes _validate_recovery_artifacts even while the live README exists; _rollback deletes it; and project_readme (readme.py:25-26) returns when README.md is not a file, so journalist-authored content is destroyed irreversibly through the public restart path. Shares one confined fix with F1 (verify original=false claims against live absence) plus a regression test forging a P7 journal and asserting the README survives.

Verified at attempts.py:29-40 — run_attempts validates only the phase name and immediately calls load_snapshot, whose durable-tree setup and atomic state write follow a symlinked root/.anomaly; the only scan (:84-86) examines the copied workspace after owner execution, so it protects neither the caller-supplied path nor the pre-execution writes. The utility is publicly documented in the installed skill and invoked directly by tests, so this is a separately reachable AC7 violation, not a dispatcher-internal shortcut. Verified at events.py: log_event builds .anomaly/events.jsonl, mkdirs parents, and opens in append mode with no containment check; the only _scan_case_tree lives in the phase_event wrapper, and test_events.py exercises bare log_event on a nonexistent case, establishing the standalone writer as supported surface. A symlinked root or .anomaly directory redirects durable event writes outside the case, and the broad never-raise handler swallows nothing here because the redirected write succeeds. causalHypotheses: Promotion-trust cluster (F1/F8/F9): _validate_recovery_artifacts encodes coherence without provenance — original=false is accepted regardless of live-file presence — while _rollback restores backups without persisting per-entry progress, so the single journalized status field must serve forgery detection, apply resumption, and rollback resumption at once and fails in both directions.

inquiry.problemRestatement: Eleven cycle-2 blockers survived refutation at hash 429c34de. Re-verified first-hand, they reduce to four roots: (a) the recovery-coherence predicate in _attempt_workspace.py both admits forged original=false journals whose rollback deletes live registry-bound artifacts (F1 data/sources.json, F9 README.md) and permanently rejects legitimately partially-rolled-back states because rollback never journalizes per-entry progress (F8) — one under-specified predicate, two failure directions; (b) whole-case no-symlink enforcement is caller-side discipline instead of a choke point on unresolved caller paths, so fork_case resolves dest before any scan (F2, duplicated as F7), run_attempts durably writes before any scan (F10), and standalone log_event mkdirs/appends through case-controlled symlinks (F11); (c) _gate_input strips the actor but never the sequence members, so whitespace-only Gate A/B IDs count as complete decisions (F3); (d) three tests prove contracts over states the pipeline cannot produce or paths it never exercises — catchable KeyboardInterrupt never reaches missing-evidence reconciliation (F4), a pending-prefix/applied-last journal contradicts sequential _apply (F5), and P7's mutation table rmtrees the whole charts directory instead of mutating a descendant (F6).
inquiry.question: Can all eleven survivors close with three bounded product sites — (1) one confined rewrite of the promotion coherence-and-rollback pair for F1/F8/F9, (2) one reuse of the existing create_case-style scan-on-unresolved-path-before-first-write at fork_case/run_attempts/log_event for F2/F7/F10/F11, (3) member blankness checks in _gate_input for F3 — plus bounded test-contract edits for F4/F5/F6, adding no new framework, runner, registry, or alias, or does any finding force more? Are these independent defects, or evidence that this part of the design should be reconstructed?

findings.summary: Registry binding still lets an untrusted promotion journal delete a legitimate phase-owned artifact by lying that it did not originally exist.
The public fork writer still follows a symlinked destination ancestor and can create the child case outside the caller-selected path.
Whitespace-only Gate A and Gate B IDs are still classified as complete human decisions.
The interrupted-attempt test never exercises restart reconciliation for a counted attempt with no failure evidence.
The claimed valid interrupted-promotion test constructs a journal state the sequential promoter cannot produce.
The P7 identity matrix does not prove that a changed chart descendant invalidates completion.

synthesis.problemRestatement: Eleven cycle-2 blockers survived refutation at gate hash 429c34de (clean, green) over the anomaly resolver-consolidation task, collapsing into four causal families on one substrate. Trust model (F1, F8, F9): _validate_recovery_artifacts checks journal schema and exact registry write-set equality but trusts the journal's own original flag about the world — a forged applied/original=false/no-backup entry passes coherence solely because the backup is absent, and _rollback deletes the live registry-bound artifact (data/sources.json; README.md, irreversibly, because project_readme returns on a missing file), all reachable through public run_workflow recovering any regular-file portable case; meanwhile _rollback consumes backups without journalizing per-entry progress and writes rolled_back once after the loop, so a second interruption mid-rollback produces an applied/original/no-backup/live shape the same validator rejects on every future restart. Containment chokepoint (F2/F7, F10, F11): whole-case no-symlink enforcement is caller-side discipline instead of a mandatory pre-write invariant — fork_case resolves dest before scanning anything, run_attempts durably writes snapshot state before its only scan (which examines the copied workspace, not the caller root documented as public utility surface), and standalone log_event mkdirs and append-opens through case-controlled symlinks unscanned. Gate validation (F3): _gate_input strips the actor but not sequence members, so whitespace-only Gate A/B IDs count as complete human decisions — Gate A burns attempts on an unknown detector, Gate B seals an empty accepted set and completes P7, violating the locked pauses-consume-no-attempts contract. Test seams (F4, F5, F6): the interrupted-attempt test only raises catchable KeyboardInterrupts whose evidence the BaseException handler persists, leaving the missing-evidence reconciliation branch unreachable; the valid-rollback fixture fabricates a pending-prefix/applied-last journal sequential _apply cannot produce; and the P7 matrix only rmtrees the whole charts directory, so recursive descendant path/kind/content hashing ships unproven.
causalHypotheses: One unstated default splits the design: durability artifacts (promotion.json, events.jsonl, state.json) and caller-supplied paths are treated as trusted internal records at some sites and untrusted input at others, wherever convenient — the recovery validator substitutes schema and registry-shape checking for provenance verification, making deletion authority forgeable (F1/F9) while producer-derived invariants simultaneously reject genuine rollback progress (F8); making the trust boundary explicit per artifact would have surfaced the entire family.

AC7's whole-case no-symlink guarantee was implemented as a library primitive (_scan_case_tree) plus per-entry-point discipline instead of a structural chokepoint on the public write API; create_case/resume_case/phase_event remember scan-unresolved-before-resolve-or-write, fork_case/run_attempts/log_event forgot it — four blockers are lapses of one architectural guarantee, not four independent bugs.

The cycle-2 seams were authored to demonstrate planned behavior rather than discriminate contract from accident: fixtures synthesize states by editing fields instead of replaying producer sequences (KeyboardInterrupt through a handler that persists evidence; a hand-built applied-last journal contradicting ordered _apply; rmtree of a whole directory that an existence-only implementation would also fail), so the suite stays green while the genuinely reachable double-interruption state deterministically bricks recovery — the seams concealed F8 rather than merely missing it.

_gate_input validates members syntactically (string, nonempty, separators, duplicates) and copies the blankness discipline onto the actor alone, omitting member.strip(), so whitespace IDs satisfy the completeness predicate and the human turn boundary silently stops pausing (F3).

src/anomaly/_attempt_workspace.py:244-264 — asymmetric coherence: non-pending original=false entries pass iff the backup is absent with NO live-absence requirement, while applied originals require backup.exists() or (applying and live.exists()); this single pair admits the F1/F9 forgery and permanently rejects F8's genuine partial-rollback shape.

Impossibility check across inquiries: the forged applied/original=false/no-backup/live-present state is extensionally identical to the legitimate outcome of promoting a brand-new artifact — README.md is genuinely first created at P7 — so the security lens's own proposed confined rule ((not original) implies not live.exists()) would also reject that genuine state; separation demands provenance or fail-closed possession rules, which is the reconstruction boundary.

src/anomaly/_attempt_workspace.py:109-136 — _rollback restores each non-pending original via backup.replace(live) with no journal write inside the loop and persists rolled_back only after the loop, so interruption mid-loop bricks every later public restart (F8); any F1/F9 fix must define its accepted-state set inside the same transition model that adds journaled restore progress, or the forgery surface reopens.

Reachability and irreversibility: src/anomaly/workflow.py:163-168 — public run_workflow resumes any regular-file portable case and calls recover_interrupted_promotion before loading state; registry tuples (workflow.py:22-83) bind data/sources.json (P1) and README.md (P7), so forged journals pass exact write-set equality; src/anomaly/readme.py:24-30 returns when README.md is absent, so rollback-deleted journalist content is never recreated.

Containment precedent is in-file, bounding the repair: case.py:104-107 create_case scans the unresolved root before resolve/write versus fork_case:166-181 resolving dest first and copytree-ing through it (F2/F7); attempts.py:35-40,82-86 run_attempts durably writes via load_snapshot before its only scan, which targets the copied workspace, while skills/anomaly/SKILL.md documents run_attempts publicly (F10); events.py:39-43 log_event mkdirs and append-opens unscanned inside a broad never-raise try that admits mapping UnsafeCasePathError to None (F11).

Seam vacuity is structural, not incidental: attempts.py:88-110 — both BaseException handlers persist failure evidence before re-raising, so tests/test_pipeline_walk.py:605-641 can never reach _reconcile_interrupted_attempt's missing-evidence branch (F4); _apply:82-104 advances strictly in registry order persisting each entry applied, making the fixture's pending-prefix/applied-last journal at :644-694 unreachable (F5); P7_OUTPUT_MUTATIONS:196-215 only rmtrees the charts directory while identities.py:78-105 hashes descendants by relative path/kind/bytes, so no row discriminates content identity from existence (F6).

Rejected alternative rationale: test-contract-repair as the selection — honest seams alone leave F1/F2/F8/F9/F10/F11 unfixed in production; unverifiable guarantees over a forgeable destructive capability do not close the union.
